description: Re-audit of the historical D56 optimized deliverable (467 routed routes) under the Phase-2 strict crossing policy, with exact and legacy sensitivity comparison; independent validator implementation four_side_1024/d56/validate_d56.py, no router code imported.

legacy.violations_note: 8919 legacy-policy violation details are omitted here; the historical sensitivity dump outputs/four_side_1024_d56_optimized/independent_audit_sensitivity_legacy.json contains the full list

strict_verdict.summary: 465 of the 467 historically routed routes remain strictly legal. Exactly one route pair, (460, 989), is illegal under strict: crossing_window_overlap. Both routes are involved in that single pair, so 465 routes pass and 2 routes fail; nothing is silently dropped. Under the historical exact policy the same 467 routes pass with zero violations.

failing_pair_analysis.explanation: Route 460's two short-S arcs (A1, A2) both cross route 989's quarter arc B1, at 19.673 deg and 16.810 deg, only 1.727 mm apart along route 460. Between the two crossings the two routes stay closer than the violation limit for a continuous 2.766 mm stretch (their separation only rises to 0.147 mm), so the exact minimal clearance-band window of each crossing contains the other crossing: the two local windows overlap completely on route 460 and by 0.345 mm on route 989. Two genuine crossings that cannot be separated into disjoint local exemption regions are exactly the 'hugging' case the strict policy rejects; the historical exact policy exempted the whole intersected primitive pairs (A1-B1, A2-B1) and therefore hid a real 2.766 mm sub-clearance run. This is one physical defect involving two routes, not two independent defects.
